findings.title: onApprove on port 3001 returns HTTP 202 without unblocking the pipeline — silent HITL deadlock
findings.detail: The port-3001 onApprove handler only calls console.error and returns normally. Any caller that sends an approve command to port 3001 instead of port 3002 receives a 202 success while the in-flight task stays permanently blocked at the HITL gate. All other daemon-only handlers (onCancel, onVerify, onForcePr) on the same server correctly throw, causing a 500 that tells the caller to re-route. onApprove does not.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace console.error(...) with throw new Error('approve(${taskId}) is daemon-only; route to CONTROL_PLANE_PORT 3002'), matching the onCancel pattern.

findings.title: npm install / yarn add / bun add / npx absent from worker deny list — shared node_modules poisoning
findings.detail: The pipeline deny list blocks pnpm install but omits npm install, yarn add, bun add, and npx. The worktree node_modules is a symlink back to the host repo, so a worker running npm install writes directly into the shared tree used by all concurrent and future tasks. An adversarially crafted task brief could exploit this to inject malicious packages.
findings.fix_sketch: Add 'Bash(npm install)', 'Bash(npm install *)', 'Bash(yarn add)', 'Bash(yarn add *)', 'Bash(bun add)', 'Bash(bun add *)', 'Bash(npx)', 'Bash(npx *)' to the deny list.

findings.title: git commit failure in editor swallowed — runner reports misleading 'no diff' instead of real error
findings.detail: The try/catch around git commit catches failure, logs console.warn, and returns normally. The caller then finds no diff (nothing committed) and logs 'possible silent tool-use failure' rather than the real error. The git add block immediately above already throws on failure with AUDIT-IFleet-e5f6a7b8; the commit block must match.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the try/catch around git commit (or rethrow). Let the rejection propagate so the pipeline surfaces the real failure message.

findings.title: discord.post_failed event appended with empty SprintId when task has no sprint — creates orphaned events
findings.detail: In daemon.ts onPostFailed, when a task has no sprintId the code falls back to '' as SprintId and writes it to the events table. These rows accumulate silently and cannot be joined to any sprint for debugging. The correct fix is to skip the event when no sprint context exists.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the orchestratorStore.appendEvent call in a guard: if (!sprintId) return; Skip the event emission entirely when the task has no sprint.

findings.title: Bandit circuit-breaker cooldown not reset when already-disabled arm receives another failure
findings.detail: In recordOutcome, when status is 'disabled' and a new failure arrives, consecutiveFailures increments but assignmentsRemaining is not reset. An arm that keeps failing while disabled will have its cooldown drain to zero early, transitioning to 'probing' before failures have actually stopped. The probe-failure path correctly resets assignmentsRemaining; the disabled-failure path must match.
findings.fix_sketch: In the else branch for status !== 'probing' and consecutiveFailures reaches threshold, also add state.assignmentsRemaining = cooldown when the arm is already disabled to refresh the window.

findings.title: trustedBrief JSON-parse block is dead code — architectOutputIsJson is always false for non-JSON briefs
findings.detail: buildBrief() always produces a markdown string for editor/reviewer/verifier roles. JSON.parse(brief) always throws for these roles, so architectOutputIsJson is always false and trustedBrief is always false. The flag is passed to adapter.spawn with no effect on the permission model in practice.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the architectOutputIsJson variable and JSON.parse block. Hardcode trustedBrief: false in the spawn call with a comment preserving the AUDIT-IFleet-6b8a5e95 reference.

findings.title: @deprecated unused octokit field still present in ForcePrDeps interface
findings.detail: The octokit?: Pick<Octokit, 'rest'> field in ForcePrDeps is annotated @deprecated unused because force-PR now routes through the PrOpener bridge. The field adds a confusing optional import and a dead code path.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the octokit field from the ForcePrDeps interface and the Octokit import if it becomes unused after removal.

findings.title: _repoRoot is a dead parameter in buildPrOpener — never referenced in function body
findings.detail: buildPrOpener(repoId, worktreePath, _repoRoot) accepts _repoRoot but never uses it. The underscore prefix signals intentional non-use, but the parameter still pollutes the signature and every call site must pass a value.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove _repoRoot from the signature and update the single call site at line 318.

findings.title: Silent fallback to gh CLI credentials when GITHUB_TOKEN is absent — no log line emitted
findings.detail: When GITHUB_TOKEN is unset, readGhAuthToken shells out to gh auth token. In a misconfigured prod environment after a secret rotation, the process silently uses personal credentials with no log entry. The fallback is only discovered when a rate-limit or permission error surfaces later.
findings.fix_sketch: Add console.warn('[github-queue] GITHUB_TOKEN not set — falling back to gh CLI credentials') before the execFileAsync call.
